title: The Principles of Wave-Particle Duality
text:
Quantum physics dictates that matter and energy exhibit both wave-like and particle-like properties. This inherent duality means that entities such as photons and electrons do not adhere strictly to classical definitions; rather, they manifest depending on the experimental context in which they are observed.

The concept of duality is vividly demonstrated by phenomena like electron diffraction, where particles create interference patterns typically associated only with continuous waves. This complexity necessitates the use of probability amplitudes (wave functions) rather than deterministic trajectories when modeling subatomic behavior.
